note: Live controls for internal/render. Re-runnable proof that these tests can fail; the closed tickets' close reasons remain the historical record.

controls.clause: A fence is a mode, not a line: an opening fence suspends every other reflow rule, blank lines included, until its matching close (dw32p.20)
A scanning verb truncates a title only when stdout is a terminal, so `drops list | grep` sees every byte (dw32p.20)
A page truncates nothing: a relation title too long for the line wraps under the id column rather than being ellipsised (dw32p.20 corrected this from the reference build)
A memory scanning result is one glyph, its measured id column, two spaces, then the title and retirement state (Should the memory verbs go through render?)
A memory listing sizes its id column to the widest permanent opaque id in the result (Should the memory verbs go through render?)
A memory scanning verb truncates display text only on a terminal and never drops bytes from a pipe (Should the memory verbs go through render?)
A tombstoned memory reports removal rather than the supersession underneath it on both human surfaces (Should the memory verbs go through render?)
A live retired memory names the memory that superseded it (Should the memory verbs go through render?)
A memory page wraps its compact identity header without truncating it (Should the memory verbs go through render?)
A memory page reflows prose bodies through the renderer's lossless body rules (Should the memory verbs go through render?)
A memory page includes non-empty provenance in its compact header (Should the memory verbs go through render?)
The human memory scanning surface routes through the injected pager (Should the memory verbs go through render?)
The human memory reading surface routes through the injected pager (Should the memory verbs go through render?)
A memory row borrows render's glyphs, so a listing and a page cannot disagree about a state (Bring cli up to the test discipline)
